newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan money rates nosedive on bank liquidation.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan money rates nosedive on bank liquidation.

text.p: Taiwan's money rates closed sharply lower on Thursday as banks rushed to liquidate excess funds on the final day of the current reserve period, dealers said.

The overnight interbank rate ended at 5.838 percent against Wednesday's 9.813 percent -- only slightly outside the central bank's 5.0-5.5 percent target zone and far below the record double-digit closes of late June.
The 30-day commercial paper also eased dramatically to 6.00-6.50 percent against 7.50-8.00 on Wednesday.

Between June 26 and July 1, Taiwan's interbank rate had spiked into double digits -- peaking at 11.325 percent at the close on Saturday -- as funds cascaded out of banks into the red-hot stock market.
Tight liquidity started to show signs of easing after the central bank's persistent fund injections through open-market operations.
Dealers said they expected the money rates to stabilise on the beginning of a new reserve period starting on Friday.
In the bond market, the benchmark 86/4 bond yield was traded at 5.8690-8700 percent compared with Wednesday's 5.8725-8730 close.
